newsitem.title: USA: Du Pont jury begins seventh day of verdict search.
newsitem.headline: Du Pont jury begins seventh day of verdict search.

text.p: Jurors in the John du Pont murder trial began their second week of deliberations on Tuesday, in a case that began with a 48-hour siege and has developed into a drawn-out conclusion.
After a sixth day of deliberations ended on Monday without result, defence attorneys began showing signs of impatience in the wait for a verdict.
Although prosecutors said there was still no cause for concern about a hung jury, their comments revealed they had begun thinking about what would be involved in a retrial.
"Is it unusual that they're out as long as they are? We think that it is," du Pont attorney Taras Wochuck told reporters on Monday after the sixth day of deliberations following Sunday's rest day.
Asked whether the defence was seeking a mistrial based on the lenghty deliberations, he said, "I'm not going to comment on that."
Prosecutors said there were no signs yet of a hung jury and jurors were still working hard.
"They haven't indicated anything to us which indicates that they've hit a wall," Delaware County District Attorney Patrick Meehan told reporters on Monday.
"Nothing has come easy in this case, and I'm optimistic," he said. "We just don't know what it is that has this jury pondering about the fate of this case."
However, Meehan said, if there were to be a retrial, finding a suitable jury may be difficult in Delaware County.

"One of the first issues that you would have to address would be whether the unique publicity in this case has somehow caused there to be a heightend awareness on the part of the potential jury pool," he said.
Du Pont, a millionaire chemicals heir, is charged with first and third-degree murder as well as voluntary manslaughter in the Jan. 26, 1996 killing of Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz.
The killing was followed by a 48-hour police standoff at du Pont's sprawling suburban Philadelphia estate.
Du Pont's lawyers have conceded du Pont killed Schultz, but are seeking a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity.
In addition to verdicts of not guilty or not guilty by reason of insanity, the jurors can render verdicts of guilty or guilty but mentally ill.
